newsitem.title: UK: Q1 profits seen up at airports operatorBAA.
newsitem.headline: Q1 profits seen up at airports operatorBAA.

text.p: British airports operator BAA Plc is expected to show profits moving ahead when it publishes first-quarter results on Tuesday, fuelled by a continuing rise in traffic.
Analysts are forecasting pre-tax profits for the three months to June 30 to rise to 134-140 million pounds from 130 million a year ago.
BAA reported last month that passenger traffic at its seven British airports rose 7.8 percent to 26.587 million passengers in the first quarter.

On Friday the share price was down 10-1/2p at 563p by 1420 GMT in a generally weaker market, but the stock has risen sharply since the UK's July 2 budget, on relief that its liability to Labour's "windfall tax" on privatised utilities was less than feared.
Management has estimated its liability at 70-100 million pounds payable over two years and told the annual meeting last month the company would fund the payments from debt.
Well-placed industry sources have told Reuters the liability is likely to be nearer 100 than 70 million pounds.
